title: Decem Theses II: Two Imperial exemplars — Wittenberg 1531 and augmented 1540/41 to Ferdinand at Naumburg 1561
pass_a_gloss: II. Meanwhile two Exemplars, properly speaking, have been acknowledged and exhibited by the Electors, Princes, and Estates of the Empire, and are to be found in the writings of Luther and Melanchthon and in the Acts of the Empire: the Earlier printed at Wittenberg in the Year 31; the Later augmented in the Years 40 and 41 and transmitted to Emperor Ferdinand I together with the earlier one at Naumburg in the Year 1561, to which up to this very day nothing has been added or taken away.
pass_b_english: II. Properly speaking, two exemplars have been acknowledged and presented by the Electors, Princes, and Imperial Estates, and they stand in Luther's and Melanchthon's writings and in the Imperial Acts.

The earlier was printed at Wittenberg in 1531; the later, enlarged in 1540 and 1541, was sent with the earlier one to Emperor Ferdinand I at Naumburg in 1561 — and to this day nothing has been added to it or taken from it.
source_text:
II.
Duo interim Exemplaria propriè loquendô ab Electoribus, Principibus & Statibus Imperii agnita & exhibita sunt, inque scriptis Lutheri & Melanchthonis & Actis Imperii reperiunda: Prius Wittenbergae An. 31. impressum; Posterius An. 40. & 41. auctum Caesarique Ferdinando I. unà cum priori, An. 1561. Naumburgô transmissum, cui ad hanc usq; diem nihil additum ademptumque fuit.
